title: Scalar extension commutes with derived singleton extension
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the module universe and let $a:B_\bullet\to C_\bullet$ be a morphism of inverse sequences of sheaves of commutative rings, commuting with all transitions [def-weil-size-convention], [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. For $R=B,C$, let $\mathscr S(R)$ be strict systems of $R_j$-module sheaves with transitions linear after scalar restriction, realized on the vertical sequence site [lem-pur-system-ringed-sequence-site], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories, exact evaluations $e_n^R$, and the derived singleton adjunctions $L_n^R\dashv e_n^R$ induced from ordinary extension [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], [lem-pur-system-level-left-extension], [lem-pur-system-single-derived-extension]. Let $S_\bullet=-\otimes^L_{B_\bullet}C_\bullet$ and $S_n=-\otimes^L_{B_n}C_n$ be change of rings, with their module-induced adjunctions to exact scalar restrictions $U_\bullet,U_n$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction].

There is a natural isomorphism of functors to $D(\mathscr S(C))$
$$d_n:S_\bullet L_n^B\xrightarrow{\sim}L_n^C S_n.$$
It is the left-adjoint conjugate of $e_n^BU_\bullet=U_ne_n^C$, for the two specified composite adjunctions, so it identifies their actual Hom transposes, units and counits. On a flat-term K-flat $B_n$-complex $Q$ [def-pc-kflat-complex], [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], the singleton extension and its scalar extension are K-flat with flat terms on their ringed sequence sites. The representative of $d_n$ at $j\le n$ is
$$(B_j\otimes_{B_n}Q)\otimes_{B_j}C_j\xrightarrow{\sim}C_j\otimes_{C_n}(Q\otimes_{B_n}C_n),\qquad (b\otimes q)\otimes c\longmapsto a_j(b)c\otimes(q\otimes1),$$
with the canonical symmetry convention for the scalar-extension factors. At $j>n$ it is the identity of zero, and at $j=n$ it is the multiplication identification. These are maps of actual system complexes and yield the displayed derived natural isomorphism, not just separate level isomorphisms. The isomorphisms commute with the canonical lower-singleton maps $L_n^R(R_n\otimes^L_{R_m}(-))\to L_m^R$ for $m\ge n$, after scalar associators. No flatness of $a_j$ or of the coefficient transitions, and no boundedness, is assumed.

proof.text: The Hom-transpose clause follows from leftAdjointUniq_homEquiv_comp after rewriting homEquiv_ofNatIsoRight_apply for the displayed derived right square.

Apply singletonSequenceOrdinary_kFlat to P over B. Apply ringed-topos K-flat pullback with the explicitly constructed identity algebraic inverse image first on the sequence site to A, then on the base site to the level scalar model. Apply singletonSequenceOrdinary_kFlat again over D to the level scalar-extended complex. This proves the six K-flatness/flat-term clauses. The singleton computes field and exact equivalence factors make its comparison invertible; scalar model computes fields make both composite comparisons invertible. The representative equation is singletonScalarDerivedIso_rep.

For the tensor formula, transpose the ordinary uniqueness component first through A and then through the sequence equivalence, yielding a strict singleton map g. Adjoint uniqueness evaluated on x identifies its nth unit value with the two target units. systemSingleTranspose and systemScalarModel_transpose_tmul express the value below n as b times the strict transition of that unit value. The target singleton transition takes its unit tensor to the unit tensor below n. The outer scalar transpose multiplies by c, and module linearity gives a_j(b)c. This proves the exact generator formula for the specified comparison, including j=n.

Above n, the target singleton level is zero by systemSingleLevelAbove, transported through the unit of the sequence equivalence. The evaluated scalar ordinary isomorphism transports this vanishing to the source, and every map from the zero source is zero.
The final lower-singleton compatibility is singletonScalarDerivedIso_lower, evaluated at n,m,h,P.
